::: {.lead}
The producer of *Night Owl Games* asks for one more loop: the music of the
calm rowing in the flood level of *Rooftop Rescue*, with a drum layer for
danger. It must loop without a gap or a click, and be ready for the game
engine. In lecture 15 you learned what loops, layers and tempo are. In
this workshop you **produce** a loop yourself: you write a short brief,
you build the loop in a step sequencer (Loop Builder, or a free music tool
in the lab), you make it seamless, and you export and check it. Every
section ends with a task, and at the end you have your own loop file.
:::

## Key terms

{{< glossary seamless-loop loop-point tempo music-bar music-layer step-sequencer adaptive-music normalize >}}

## 16.1 Plan: the brief

A loop starts with a few decisions, written down before the first note:
the **brief** (@fig-brief).

::: {.callout-important title="Definition 16.1 — The brief of a loop"}
A loop brief answers five questions: **mood** (how should the player
feel?), **tempo** (BPM), **length** (a whole number of bars), **layers**
(which play always, which only for some states) and **file** (format, name,
level).
:::

![The brief of the rowing loop.](images/loop-brief.png){#fig-brief width=94%}

::: {.callout-note title="Example 16.1 — Two briefs"}
1. Rowing: calm, a little sad, with hope; 100 BPM; 8 bars (19.2 s);
   melody and bass, drums only for danger; `mus_rowing_calm_loop.ogg`.
2. Menu: friendly and light; 120 BPM; 4 bars (8 s); melody, bass and soft
   hats; `mus_menu_loop.ogg`.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistake"}
Starting to click notes without a brief. The loop then has no clear mood,
and its length is not planned in bars.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Write your brief"}
Choose one moment of a game (a menu, a calm level, a chase) and write the
five lines of its brief.

*Your result:* a brief of five lines.
:::

## 16.2 Build the loop in a step sequencer

A **step sequencer** shows one bar as a grid: one row per sound, 16 steps
per bar. You turn cells on and off and hear the result at once.

::: {.callout-important title="Definition 16.2 — Building in layers"}
Build the loop **layer by layer**: first the rhythm (kick on beats 1 and 3,
snare on 2 and 4), then the bass (a few long notes), then the melody (a
short phrase that can repeat). Keep the calm layers simple, and put the
energy into the layers for the danger state.
:::

{{< sim file="sims/loop-builder.html" poster="sims/loop-builder.png" title="Loop Builder: a game-music loop in 16 steps" height="760" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Example 16.2 — Yara's rowing loop"}
1. Tempo 100 BPM.
2. Bass: C on beat 1, A on beat 3: slow and calm.
3. Melody: five notes (E, G, A, G, E) in the first half of the bar, silence
   in the second half: the phrase can breathe.
4. Drums for danger: kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4, hats on every
   eighth. In calm they are muted.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistake"}
Filling every cell. A full grid sounds busy and tiring, especially in a
calm loop. Leave space: silence is part of the music.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Build your loop"}
1. In **Loop Builder** (press Clear first), build your loop from your
   brief: rhythm, bass, then melody.
2. Switch between calm and chase. Do both states fit their moments?

*Your result:* a loop that you can play in both states.
:::

## 16.3 Make it seamless and export it

A loop is ready only when its end joins its start without a gap or a click
(@fig-seam), and when the file fits the game.

::: {.callout-important title="Definition 16.3 — A seamless, game-ready loop"}
- The loop is a **whole number of bars** long.
- At the **loop point** the wave goes smoothly from the end to the start: no
  silence (cut it) and no jump (a few milliseconds of fade, or a cut at
  zero).
- A sound that rings over the end (a tail) is mixed into the start.
- The peaks stay near −6 dB, so that effects and voices have room.
- Export: WAV for work, OGG for the game; a clear name with the tempo.
:::

![A gap, a click and a seamless loop.](images/seamless-loop.png){#fig-seam width=94%}

::: {.callout-note title="Example 16.3 — Exporting the rowing loop"}
1. Yara downloads the WAV from Loop Builder: her 1-bar pattern 4 times,
   so 4 bars, 9.6 s at 100 BPM.
2. In Audacity, she repeats it once (Effect › Repeat): 8 bars, 19.2 s. She
   checks the join with loop play (the loop button, or Shift + Space) and
   listens 10 times.
3. She normalizes the peaks to −6 dB and exports
   `mus_rowing_calm_loop_100bpm.ogg`.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistake"}
Checking a loop by playing it once. Most loop problems are heard only at
the second and third repeat. Always loop-play it many times.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Export and check"}
1. Download your loop (Download WAV) or record it in Audacity.
2. In Audacity, loop-play it 10 times. Is there a gap or a click?
3. Export it with a good name, with the tempo.

*Your result:* one loop file with a good name.
:::

## Case study: Loop Doctor

Students sent their loops for *Rooftop Rescue*, and each one has a
problem: a click at the loop point; a length of 7.5 bars at 100 BPM; a
reverb tail with silence at the end; a calm loop with drums, a fast melody
and a loud bass; a loop that peaks at 0 dB; and a good loop that still
needs a file name. The Game challenge of the interactive lesson uses these
loops. In the mini-game below you choose the fix for each one.

## Further reading

Audacity Manual, "Looping" and "Loop Play". Collins, *Game Sound* (2008),
Chapter 8. Unity Manual, "Audio Clip" (the Loop setting).

## Exercises

1. Name the five lines of a loop brief.
2. In which order do you build the layers?
3. Where do the kick and the snare usually play in a 4-beat bar?
4. Why should a calm loop not fill every cell?
5. How long are 4 bars at 120 BPM?
6. What causes a click at the loop point, and how do you fix it?
7. What do you do with a tail that rings over the end of the loop?
8. Why should the music peak near −6 dB?
9. How do you check a loop in Audacity?
10. Write a good file name for a menu loop at 120 BPM.

## Answers to the exercises

::: {.answers}
1. Mood, tempo, length, layers, file.
2. Rhythm, bass, melody.
3. Kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4.
4. A full grid sounds busy and tiring.
5. 8 s.
6. A jump in the wave; a short fade or a cut at zero.
7. Mix it into the start of the loop.
8. To leave room for effects and voices.
9. With loop play, listening many times.
10. `mus_menu_loop_120bpm.ogg`.
:::
